package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious Windows DLL, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: UNAPIMON is a DLL malware used for DLL hijacking and API unhooking to evade monitoring of child processes. It is designed to facilitate defense evasion and enable further malicious activity by preventing security tools from observing process behavior.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the DLL is loaded via hijacking or side-loading)
execution_context.file_location: Malicious DLL file (e.g., loaded in place of a legitimate DLL by a vulnerable application)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime (DLL load), the code restores original bytes of critical Windows API functions in ntdll.dll, removing userland hooks placed by security products, so that subsequent process and memory operations are not monitored.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unhooking APIs in ntdll.dll is a well-known technique used by malware to evade detection by security products that rely on userland hooks to monitor process activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLLs do not attempt to unhook or tamper with system API functions in memory. This behavior is only expected in advanced malware or red team tools.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some security or anti-cheat software may use similar techniques to protect themselves from tampering, but this is rare and typically well-documented.
key_indicators: Restoration of syscall stubs for process/memory APIs

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the DLL is loaded via hijacking/side-loading)
execution_context.file_location: Malicious DLL file (replaces or is loaded alongside a legitimate DLL in a trusted application directory)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime (DLL load via hijacking), the code executes malicious payload logic in the context of a trusted process, potentially enabling privilege escalation, persistence, or further defense evasion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLL hijacking is a common technique for executing malicious code under the guise of a legitimate process, often bypassing application whitelisting and security controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLLs do not appear unexpectedly in application directories or execute unauthorized code during process attach.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, legitimate software may use DLL proxying for compatibility, but this is not common and is usually documented.
key_indicators: DLL loaded from non-standard or writable directory

attack_chain.action: Malicious DLL is placed in a directory where a trusted application will load it (DLL hijacking/side-loading).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious DLL is loaded by the application, triggering code execution.

attack_chain.action: Upon loading, the DLL executes its malicious payload, including API unhooking to evade monitoring.
attack_chain.leads_to: Subsequent malicious actions (e.g., process injection, credential theft) are performed without being detected by security tools.

behavioral_signatures: DLL loaded from non-standard or user-writable directories
Memory modification of ntdll.dll or other system DLLs to restore original API bytes
Execution of code in DllMain that is not present in the legitimate DLL
file_indicators: DLL files with names matching legitimate system or application DLLs but located in unexpected directories
network_indicators: N/A (UNAPIMON itself does not perform network activity, but may enable follow-on malware that does)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for DLLs loaded from non-standard or user-writable directories, especially those with names matching legitimate system DLLs. Detect memory modifications to ntdll.dll or restoration of syscall stubs at runtime. Alert on unexpected code execution in DllMain or DLLs that are not part of the official application distribution. Correlate with known malicious hashes and YARA rules for API unhooking techniques.
